title: Opus, Fable, Astra, Sol - Create a Scene with a 45 Minute Time Requirement
author: 314t
selftext:
Another non-scientific experiment involving Opus, Fable, Astra and Sol, all at medium effort but this time they were ALL required to work for at LEAST 45 minutes. Usually I see these models at medium complete their tasks in 5 to 30 minutes. So what happens when you give them a strict requirement to run for 45 minutes?

Surprised they all complied with the time requirement, Opus was the only one to go over the time, but there was no max

  
Who cooked in your opinion?

**PROMPT:**  
Build an explorable Victorian greenhouse in a lunar crater scene. Outside: grey dust, sharp shadows, a black sky, and Earth overhead. Inside: dense plants, warm lanterns, mist, and condensation running down the glass. Bootprints lead to the door, with an antique diving suit slumped on a bench beside it. Only the interior moves; outside stays completely still.

Use retrieved assets, cinematic lighting, and first-person controls. Spend at least 45 minutes building and refining it.

comments.author: taisui
comments.body: Claude models have better understanding of the environment, ChatGPT models have better understanding of individual things.

replies.author: 314t
replies.body: Wonder if I can refine these tests? Like maybe have codex add one thing at a time in separate sessions? Thoughts?

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body:
Telling AI to do something in a certain time frame is stupid.

AI doesn't feel time. It can read time stamps but it doesn’t think "oh shit 10 minutes left, gotta work harder and faster".

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: It can read time stamps, and it can interpret goals, so yeah it does "think" that.  That would be part of the reasoning chain.
